reasons: Deviation classification is sound: original 4(a) vests the Works in Company only 'to the extent' the relevant period has been invoiced and paid, with no present assignment and no interim licence, so any unbilled/unpaid/disputed period leaves commissioned work product with Contractor and no rights back — below the fallback, which requires a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables. The document also lacks any Customer Data / Company pre-existing materials ownership statement.

Redline is valid and directionally correct: it converts ownership into a present, irrevocable assignment on creation expressly decoupled from invoicing/payment, and adds a Company-retains-rights-in-its-data-and-materials sentence, with Contractor's background IP (4(b)) and the perpetual sublicensable licence-back (4(c)) untouched — exactly the redline guidance (reverse/complete the assignment, add the Customer Data sentence).

The failed 'minimal edit' heuristic (0.82 changed-character ratio) is acceptable here: the payment-conditioned ownership trigger cannot be neutralised without rewriting the operative sentence, and the edit preserves the surrounding definitional language and the trailing further-assurances clause.

Comment is accurate, concise, in-voice, cites the playbook position, and correctly notes that 4(b)/4(c) are unchanged while offering payment-protection alternatives; the rationale properly downgrades the licence-back's silence on irrevocability to a note rather than a second flag.

Minor gap (not fatal): Section 4(d)'s deferral of modification rights until payment in full is criticised in the rationale but left unredlined; the added present assignment of all right, title and interest should override it, but a short conforming edit to 4(d) (deleting the payment/termination precondition) would close the residual inconsistency.
